record.paper_title: Banach spaces and Ramsey Theory: some open problems
record.original_question: For each positive integer n, let R_n^∞ be the maximum Banach–Mazur distance d_BM(X, ℓ_∞^n) over all n-dimensional Banach spaces X. Determine the asymptotic behavior of R_n^∞ as n tends to infinity.

evidence.quote: Problem 1. (Distance from the cube – A. Pe lczy´nski [65]) Determine the asymp￾totic behavior of Rn∞ as n tends to infinity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For real Banach spaces $X$ and $Y$ of the same finite dimension, the Banach–Mazur distance is defined by
$$d_{BM}(X,Y) = \inf\{\,\|T\|\cdot\|T^{-1}\| : T:X\to Y \text{ is a linear isomorphism}\,\}.$$
For each positive integer $n$, let $\ell_\infty^n$ denote $\mathbb{R}^n$ equipped with the norm $\|x\|_\infty = \max_{1\le i\le n}|x_i|$, and define
$$R_n^\infty \;=\; \sup\{\, d_{BM}(X,\ell_\infty^n) : X \text{ is an } n\text{-dimensional real Banach space}\,\}.$$
Determine the asymptotic behavior of $R_n^\infty$ as $n\to\infty$. In particular, find matching upper and lower bounds, up to constants or up to the correct power of $n$, for the rate of growth of $R_n^\infty$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, due to Pełczyński, remains open. The best known lower bound is of order $\sqrt{n}$ (via the projection constant of $\ell_1^n$), while the best known upper bound is $R_n^\infty \le C\, n^{5/6}$, established by Bourgain–Szarek and refined through the Dvoretzky–Rogers factorization (Szarek–Talagrand, Giannopoulos). The exact asymptotic order has not been determined.

status_evidence.title: The Banach-Mazur distance to the cube and the Dvoretzky-Rogers factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Distance of every n-dimensional normed space from ℓ_∞^n is at most (2n)^{5/6}.
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is of order n^{5/6}.

status_evidence.title: Restricted Invertibility and the Banach-Mazur distance to the cube
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the Banach–Mazur distance to the cube; lower bounds related to projection constants.
status_evidence.claim: Lower bound of order sqrt(n) is the best known.

status_evidence.title: On the Banach–Mazur Distance in Small Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Pełczyński asked what is the order of the maximal possible Banach–Mazur distance to the cube.
status_evidence.claim: The exact asymptotic remains an open problem of Pełczyński.
